issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may set aside an order granting anticipatory bail when the court granting it failed to consider material evidence and relevant factors bearing on the seriousness of the offence and the accused’s alleged role.
material_facts: The appeals challenged orders granting anticipatory bail in a serious offence involving a murder.
The FIR and witness statements attributed specific roles to the applicants in the incident.

The High Court relied on an investigation report finding that the applicants were not present, but did not address identified deficiencies in that investigation, including its failure to account for eyewitness statements and its reliance on incomplete or unverified material.

A Magistrate had identified deficiencies in the investigation and directed further investigation; the High Court did not adequately consider those circumstances or the allegations against the applicants.
issues.conclusion: The anticipatory bail orders were set aside because the High Court had overlooked material aspects, including the gravity of the offence and the specific allegations against the applicants.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, anticipatory bail is discretionary and must be considered in light of factors including the nature and gravity of the offence and the role attributed to the applicant. Under Mahipal v. Rajesh Kumar, an appellate challenge to an order granting bail asks whether the order reflects an improper, arbitrary, perverse, illegal or unjustified exercise of discretion, including non-application of mind to relevant material; this differs from cancellation based on later misconduct or supervening circumstances. The Court also relied on Neeru Yadav v. State of U.P. for that distinction, Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Dr. Naresh Kumar Mangla v. Anita Agarwal for the factors relevant to anticipatory bail and appellate review, and Pokar Ram v. State of Rajasthan for considerations governing anticipatory bail.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_anticipatory_bail_grant and serious_offence and specific_role_allegations and material_evidence_ignored

predicates.appeal_challenges_anticipatory_bail_gran: A party appeals an order granting a person release on bail in anticipation of arrest.
predicates.serious_offence: The alleged offence is serious in nature.
predicates.specific_role_allegations: The available complaint or witness accounts attribute a specific role in the alleged offence to the person granted bail.
predicates.material_evidence_ignored: The court granting bail does not address material evidence or relevant circumstances bearing on the alleged offence or the person's role.
predicates.anticipatory_bail_grant_set_aside: The order granting bail in anticipation of arrest is set aside.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges an anticipatory bail grant and the alleged offence is serious, specific roles are alleged, and material evidence is ignored, the grant is set aside.
